title: The Line Is the Product: How FOMO Sells Presale Condos, and How It Ends
seoTitle: The Line Is the Product: FOMO in Presale Real Estate
description: A long line outside a club makes you want in. Why presale demand works the same way, who formed the Toronto line, and what happens when it shrinks.
answer: In presale real estate, the line is the product. Buyers join a project because others are already waiting, not because they have seen what is inside. That fear of missing out drove Toronto presales for years, when investors were 70% or more of buyers. When the line gets shorter, the same instinct works in reverse and buyers leave.
keywords: fear of missing out real estate
body:
Why do people buy a home that does not exist yet? Often for the same reason they join a line outside a nightclub.

## The nightclub test

Picture a club with a long line outside. You cannot hear the music. You have no idea who is inside. But the line is long, so you join it. If so many people are waiting, it must be good. That instinct has a name: FOMO, the fear of missing out. And it carries a secret that every presale launch depends on. The line is the product.

## Who stood in the Toronto line

For years, the presale line in Toronto was made mostly of investors. A study by Urbanation and CIBC found they were 70% or more of presale buyers. They were not buying a place to live. They were buying the belief that the building would go up in value. A line like that looks strong, but it only holds while the numbers work.

## When the line gets shorter

Now picture the line a little shorter one night, and shorter again the next. Then people start walking out of the club, because nobody wants to be the last one on the dance floor when the lights come on. FOMO works in both directions. The same fear that pulls buyers in pushes them out once others leave first.

That is what happened in Toronto. Rates rose, rents stopped covering mortgages, and the line went home. New condo sales fell to the lowest level since 1991.

## What to look at instead

Before you join a line, ask who is standing in it. A line of people who plan to live in the building is very different from a line of investors waiting for a price jump. In my experience, that one question tells you how long the music will keep playing. This is my opinion, not financial advice.

This clip comes from a longer episode about who creates off-plan believers and five signs a storm is coming. Listen to the full episode at [/podcast/off-plan-runs-on-believers-here-is-how-it-breaks/](/podcast/off-plan-runs-on-believers-here-is-how-it-breaks/).
takeaways: Presale buyers often join because others are already waiting.
Fear of missing out pulls buyers in and pushes them out just as fast.
Toronto presale demand relied on investors who were 70% or more of buyers.
Ask who makes up the line before you join it.
faq: What is FOMO in real estate?
FOMO, the fear of missing out, is when buyers commit because many others are buying, not because of what the property offers.
Why is an investor-heavy presale market risky?
Investors buy for appreciation. When rents stop covering mortgages or prices stall, they stop buying at the same time, and demand can disappear quickly.
What share of Toronto presale buyers were investors?
A study by Urbanation and CIBC found that investors made up 70% or more of presale condo buyers in the Toronto region.
